This game is great in so many areas, but there's one thing that killed it for me: Trait points capped.

Unlike the previous game, which had unlimited trait points, this one has a cap of 65. So you can max out 6.5 skill trees before you can't progress anymore. So after a playthrough and some multiplayer sessions, I'm capped out.

In the previous game, you could keep re-rolling your campaign and keep helping friends and strangers on bosses and keep leveling up and being incentivized to keep playing and beating the same bosses sometimes. But in this game, unless it's a new boss or a new area, I have no reason to play it, and you find yourself in the same area a lot.

They recently raised the cap from 60 to 65, but that's not enough. It's not a PvP game. Me leveling up after putting hours in should be allowed. And unlike the last game, there's not many traits, and the ones they do have aren't very good.

I cautiously recommend the game. 
Absolutely loved From the Shadows, so when 2 was announced I was very excited. Finally got the game before launch thanks to the special edition and started playing immediately and I am having a lot of fun.
The caution is here to warn about some pretty severe issues my friends and I have with the game as it currently is. The developers are very active online in the community discussing changes and fixes and thats truly awesome. A really great team over there really putting the effort in.
Unfortunately I'll probably be taking a break from the game for a while because there are just too many issues at the moment. My main complaints being the trait system limitations, armor being completely useless with no way to upgrade it, the lack of weapon and world variety, and the seriously poor balance when playing solo vs with friends, as well as the poor balance between different weapons, archetypes, and mods. They made a bunch of changes from the first game in an attempt to avoid everyone using the same things, and inadvertently pushed everyone into using the same things, because there are now outright best things to use. Best weapons, best archetypes, best mods, etc. There are entire playstyles that are just not viable for solo play, or not viable for an entire world you visit. I also personally feel that the boss design in this game leaves a lot to be desired compared to From the Ashes (but I guess thats an unpopulat opinion lmao)

Regardless, the worlds are great, the enemy variety is definitely there, and overall the game is very fun and full of things to do. I recommend picking this one up and playing a bit while the devs are hard at work making it the best it can possibly be.

If you're looking for Remant: From the Ashes, this isn't it. While the game looks nice, I've spent many hours on the first game and at 20 hours I've realized a few things.

* We just hit the final boss yesterday. After looking up all the available weapons we are missing about 80% of them. This isn't like the first game or like dark souls where you get a choice between a boss weapon or a mod,  90% of the mains story bosses drop mods and not weapons.
* If you don't play with a guide doing everything step by step you miss out of 80% of the game. We have been following the mains story, branching off to everything we can find. Which come to find out playing just the story and immediate side quests results in pretty much nothing. No cool weapons, at all.
* There is so much dialogue choices for every single NPC I just dont understand how the first game was awesome, in your face while this one has you reading books everywhere, NPCs is way too much to say with little to no impact on the game or your decisions, and it overall feels like a chore to slog through it all.
* I can't fathom the design to put weapons and gear through muddled secrets that you would need to pull up guides for every step if the way. We ACCIDENTALLY found a gun with some beacon side quest which we could have screwed up at any time. If i spend 20 minutes in a boss fight who has a really neat looking weapon and move-set to come out with a mod that shoots tentacles then it wasn't worth it.
* Were going through on veteran because the Nightmare wasn't available until you finish the game. Thank god for that or else we probably wouldn't have figured out how not fun and cool this game which we though was just going to be a beefed up Remnant:n From the Ashes to such a disappointing slog.
* Bosses are insanely aggravating and I've finished every dark souls/demons souls. Those games make you understand your weakness. This game makes you think you're doing the right thing putting points in a useless slot only to find that their attack hit-boxes are far bigger that they show on screen, oh and they will non stop swing until you're dead with no interruptions. I can't learn from bad design.
* There "hidden" classes that you have to do some arbitrary nonsense that no casual or sane gamer would ever figure out. I paid for a game and have to play "lets watch a YouTube to find out how to do this" instead of just enjoying my play-through.

This isn't on the same level as the first game. Knowing what i know now I would have skipped this and went and replayed the first one. I kept telling myself "next boss will have a weapon" over and over again until there wasn't anymore bosses left to get to through what I can only assume a normal person who buys the game will encounter.

It's a shame. This was on my radar the moment it was announced and I wish I could refund the copies I bought for me and a friend. After 20 hours of saying "next one will be the turning point" it just never delivered.

TL;DR: Overall, 9.6/10. After about 34 hours in the game, I can say Remnant II is worth playing for its refreshingly unique worlds, deep, philosophical story, and fun co-op gameplay. Another great true co-op from Gunfire Games!

Story: 10/10
World: 10/10
Character Customization: 9/10
User Interface: 9/10
Gameplay & Controls: 9/10
Graphics & Sound Design: 10/10
NPCs & Mobs: 10/10
Co-op: 10/10
Bug-free: 9/10

STORY: Poetically, deeply told, just like the first one. Beautiful. It takes place after the story of the first, making it a sequel, which is really cool! We get to see familiar faces, just older now. I love the depth of characters, the prose of the writing itself, the uniqueness of the plot and elements therein. Well done.

WORLD: As presaged by its predecessor, again so inventive. Though not as breathtaking as the first one was for the first time (what is, for the second time?), incredibly beautiful and unique. Like nothing you've ever seen - unless of course you've played the first one. But even that is different from this game.

CHARACTER CUSTOMIZATION: Still not as good as it could be, Remnant II's character creator is better than its prequel. I'd say the characters look even better than the first one, which is to be expected. There still aren't a ton of options, so if you're looking for a game with lots of customization, this isn't it - but it's enough for me to make a unique character I like looking at the entire playthrough.

UI: Beautiful and clean! Again, it's how I remember it from the first game. The map isn't great though, same as From the Ashes.

GAMEPLAY & CONTROLS: Pretty much the same as the first game. Actions and movement like dodging are a little slow for my liking, but not game breaking and certainly makes you strategize better. As always, the firearms feel and sound good to shoot, the melee weapons are fun (they added a staff!!), and mods are useful. One critique I have is that there just doesn't seem to be a way to upgrade armor anymore, and stats of new armor you get aren't any better than the starter gear, which feels a little unsatisfying and doesn't make me want to grind for new stuff like we did in the first game.

Really loved playing as the Handler. The dog's coding is actually pretty good - stayed out of my way, did a ♥♥♥♥ ton of damage, and could even revive me and/or teammates. Such a useful guy to have around. And he's cute! He'll crouch when you crouch :D

GRPAHICS & SOUND DESIGN: Beautiful game! I wouldn't call it the most beautiful game I've ever played, but it's always lovely to look at. The sounds are really cool, just like the first game - very creepy when they should be, awe-inspiring, intriguing, terrifying, at the appropriate times. Really sets the right ambiance for each area.

NPCs & MOBS: So unique and exciting. No two NPCs are the same, and it is so interesting to hear their deep, expertly crafted stories. They feel like real people with the diversity and variety you'd expect from totally different societies. SO refreshing! Even the mobs are interesting to fight because they're all different. Boss fights are always an exercise of the mind as well as just a blast.

CO-OP: This game is so much fun with friends. You can play solo too, but I prefer co-op - and it's TRUE co-op! No invasions, no ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, easy joining to or from friends' worlds...this studio knows what true co-op is and implements it so well.

BUG-FREE: Actually, this second installment is an improvement over the first. I haven't run into any bugs at all yet.

Edit 12/16/2023
Still the worst $50 I ever spent on this platform.  Game is still irritating ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Multiplayer is always garbage/dead/unavailable.  Controls are still finicky ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Gameplay is unrewarding.  I only die due to controls not responding or enemies spawning 10 feet behind me.  

Quick Summary:  2.5/10
1) Character customization (physical):  Dogsh*t.  Afterthought.  Doesn't matter.
2) Character customization (skills & Talents):  Meh. Basic.  Leveling is mostly unrewarding 75% of the time.
3) Difficulty: Typical dark souls experience.
4) Online play:  ABSOLUTE dogsh*t.  The worst aspect of the game, and the most disappointing.  Forced spectating.  Disconnections.  Joining a game where the host is AFK.  Just awful.
5) Graphics and design:  Really phenomenal, even if some areas are ripped from Stranger Things.
6) Weapons and armor:  Extremely lackluster.  Same systems are Dark Souls, except armor is RARE.

Long summary:

Hey Gunfire Games.  It appears you're trying to make a game.  I presume you want it to be enjoyable.  Here are some tips from someone who actually plays video games that maybe you can use for Remnant 3:

Good idea:  Make boss kills feel rewarding by having them drop unique weapons and armor.
Bad idea:  Not having bosses drop anything useful at all, ever.

Good idea:  Character customization.
Bad idea:  Have everyone look identical, man or woman, if they are wearing the same armor.  Sh*t, just pay a nerd who mods for Skyrim to show you how.

Good idea:  Allow players to use an arsenal of different skills that they can combine to form their own unique playstyle.
Bad idea:  Only allow players 1 ability to use at a time.

Good idea:  When a player levels up, reward them with something.  Anything.  Seriously, literally anything is good.
Bad idea:  Making leveling up completely pointless by not rewarding the player with anything.

Good idea:  Have fun, enjoyable online Coop where the players have multiple ways to aid each other and work together.  (Left 4 Dead 2, Vermintide, etc)
Bad idea:  Have online Coop where you wait in spectator mode for 15 minutes while the active player finishes killing a boss, then they quit and you get disconnected.

Those are the big ones.  I figured you guys could use some advice from someone who actually plays video games.  If you want Remnant 3 to be an overwhelming success, feel free to follow my guide here.  Good luck in the future.

This game is amazing, I haven't been this excited and invested since Remnant 1,

Games like... okay i guess. I feel like there are a lot of things that the game could improve on such as fixing achievements (they are just really glitched for no reason), making farming easier or more rewarding, adding a stats page to tell you how many aberrations you've killed (I swear i killed more than 25 when i got the achievement), making armor actually useful, making later game weapons feel powerful, and probably some more that i can't think of. 

Anyway, despite all the negatives, after  I realized that I can turn the difficulty of my world down to survivor after trying veteran for my first run, this game got really fun. I think one of the most interesting things about this game is the procedural generation that all the worlds have. There are 2 main stories for each of the 3 starting worlds which made replaying this game for achievements a lot more fun than others because it actually feels like a different world. sorry to look at all the negatives but weapons were quite disappointing as the only way to get a stronger weapon is to just upgrade your base weapon. I used the same secondary weapon which I got at the beginning for the entire game because it just felt stronger than anything else. I still had fun with the 5 total weapons i used throughout the entire game but still left something to be desired. Back to the goods. All of the world bosses were very fun to learn the attack patterns of and it felt satisfying to shmurder them.

tldr: there are some problems with game, but overall game pretty fun still
